basic_information.short_title: Extension of the 2022 Appropriations, and Quarterly Reporting
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE AVAILABILITY OF THE GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS ACT OF THE BANGSAMORO UNTIL DECEMBER 31, 2023, EXCEPT PERSONNEL SERVICES, AND GENERAL ADMINISTRATION AND SUPPORT UNDER MAINTENANCE AND OTHER OPERATING EXPENSES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 48 AND 67 OF THE GENERAL PROVISIONS OF THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 23 OR FY 2022 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS ACT OF THE BANGSAMORO
basic_information.session: First Regular Session, Second Bangsamoro Transition Authority (begun 19 Safar 1444 / 15 September 2022)
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: Immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Extends the 2022 Bangsamoro budget to the end of 2023 — and rewrites the reporting rules so ministries must publish quarterly financial and physical reports on their own websites, with an automatic salary suspension for officials who do not.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The 2022 appropriations were about to lapse. Parliament used the same act to tighten the accountability provisions of that budget, adding publication duties and a real sanction for missing them.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Most 2022 money stayed obligable to 31 December 2023, with infrastructure payable to 30 June 2024. Unreleased appropriations lapse and unspent funds revert to the Bangsamoro Treasury under a Special Fund. Ministries must file quarterly reports within 30 days of each quarter — electronically, in hard copy, and on their website — and copy them to Parliament.
who_will_be_affected: Anyone tracking how the Bangsamoro Government spends money — the reports must be public
Ministry and office heads, who are responsible for compliance
Officials and employees who fail to report, whose salaries are automatically suspended
Constituent LGUs, whose share of income taxes collected in the BARMM had its own extended window
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Took effect immediately on publication in early 2023. The reporting duties it inserted continue to apply to the 2022 budget's general provisions.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. The 2022 budget ran to the end of 2023 — and every ministry must publish quarterly financial and physical reports. Miss them and the responsible official's salary is automatically suspended until they comply.
in_practice: Most 2022 appropriations obligable to 31 December 2023; Personnel Services and General Administration and Support under MOOE excluded
Infrastructure capital outlays: obligable to 31 December 2023, construction completed, inspected and paid by 30 June 2024
Other MOOE and capital outlay items: delivery, inspection and payment by 31 March 2024
Unreleased appropriations lapse; unexpended funds revert to the Bangsamoro Treasury under a Special Fund for reappropriation
Quarterly reports due within 30 days of each quarter's end, via the Unified Reporting System, in hard copy to MFBM, and on the ministry's own website
Copies furnished to Parliament and to the Chair of the Committee on Finance, Budget and Management

for_specific_groups.Citizens and journalists: Section 2 is the useful one — quarterly financial and physical accomplishment reports must be posted on each ministry's website, not merely filed internally.
for_specific_groups.Ministry and office heads: The Minister or Head of Office is made responsible for ensuring compliance with the penalty provision.
for_specific_groups.Officials who miss reports: Salaries are automatically suspended until they comply; repeated failure without justifiable cause may be a ground for administrative disciplinary action.
for_specific_groups.Constituent LGUs: The share of income taxes collected within the BARMM had its own disbursement window to 31 December 2023.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: All Bangsamoro ministries and offices under the FY2022 budget.
what_you_can_do: Look for the quarterly financial and physical reports on the ministry's website — publication there is required
Ask the Committee on Finance, Budget and Management, which must be furnished a copy
Note the 30-day deadline after each quarter when checking whether a report is late
watch_out_for: The salary suspension is automatic on the face of the act, but it runs 'pursuant to Section 57, Chapter 6, Book VI of E.O. 292, as may be applicable' — so the national civil service framework governs how it actually bites.
Compliance is dated from the ministry's own written notice that a report has been submitted or posted.
This act does not itself publish anything; it obliges ministries to.

key_terms_explained.Obligation: Committing money to a contract or purchase, as distinct from paying it out.
key_terms_explained.Reversion: Unspent money going back to the Treasury, here into a Special Fund for reappropriation under Section 19, Article XII of the Organic Law.
key_terms_explained.URS: Unified Reporting System — the electronic channel for submitting government reports.
key_terms_explained.E.O. 292: The national Administrative Code of 1987, whose Section 57, Book VI covers withholding of salaries for unsubmitted reports.
key_terms_explained.Physical accomplishment: What was actually built or delivered, as opposed to what was spent.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Jumada Al-Awwal 28, 1444 / 22 December 2022, approved by the Chief Minister on Jumada Al-Akhirah 19, 1444 / 12 January 2023.

benefits.headline: Quarterly spending reports published on ministry websites, with salaries suspended for non-compliance.

direct_benefits.benefit: Quarterly financial and physical reports published on each ministry's website
direct_benefits.how_to_access: The ministry's own website, within 30 days of each quarter's end

direct_benefits.benefit: Reports furnished to Parliament and to the Finance Committee chair
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Members of Parliament and, through them, the public
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Via the Committee on Finance, Budget and Management

direct_benefits.benefit: An enforceable sanction — automatic salary suspension until compliance
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Everyone relying on the reports existing
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Applied by the Minister or Head of Office

indirect_benefits: A clear rule that unspent money reverts to the Treasury rather than lingering
Extended windows so 2022-funded infrastructure could be completed and paid
limitations: The salary sanction operates through the national civil service framework, not by this act alone.
No penalty falls on a ministry that publishes late but before challenge.
The act does not require the reports to be in any particular format.

for_citizens: None. The duties fall on ministries and offices.
for_ministries: Submit quarterly financial and physical reports within 30 days of each quarter's end
Submit through the Unified Reporting System, in hard copy to MFBM, and on the ministry's website
Furnish a copy to Parliament and to the Chair of the Committee on Finance, Budget and Management
Send written notice that reports have been submitted or posted

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts for the public. Its restriction falls on officials: failing to submit the required quarterly reports.

penalties.for_officials: Automatic suspension of the salaries of the responsible official or employee until they comply, pursuant to Section 57, Chapter 6, Book VI of Executive Order 292. Repeated failure or refusal without justifiable cause may be a ground for administrative disciplinary action under civil service rules.
penalties.note: The Minister or Head of Office is expressly made responsible for ensuring compliance with this penalty provision.

where_to_complain.oversight: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management, which receives the hard copies; and the Parliament's Committee on Finance, Budget and Management, which must be furnished copies
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no citizen complaints procedure, but it does create documents a citizen can ask for.

everyday_scenarios: A resident wants to know what a ministry actually built with its 2022 budget. Section 2 requires quarterly physical as well as financial accomplishment reports, posted on the ministry's website within 30 days of each quarter.
A ministry misses two quarters. The responsible official's salary is automatically suspended until the reports are filed, and repeated refusal can become an administrative disciplinary matter.
A contractor finishing a 2022-funded road has until 30 June 2024 for completion, inspection and payment.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Amends Section 48 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 23 (the FY2022 General Appropriations Act). All appropriations except Personnel Services and General Administration and Support under MOOE are available for release and disbursement until 31 December 2023, as is the amount appropriated as the constituent LGUs' share of income taxes collected within the BARMM. After the validity period, unreleased appropriations lapse and unexpended or undisbursed funds revert to the Bangsamoro Treasury under a Special Fund for reappropriation under Section 19, Article XII of RA 11054; ministries and offices must strictly observe validity and reversion. FY2022 infrastructure capital outlays are obligable to 31 December 2023 with completion of construction, inspection and payment by 30 June 2024; MOOE and other capital outlay items are obligable to 31 December 2023 with delivery, inspection and payment by 31 March 2024. Personnel Services remain valid only until 31 December 2022.

Section 2 — Amends Section 67 of BAA 23 on Quarterly Financial and Physical Reports. Ministries and offices must submit quarterly reports on their financial and physical accomplishments within 30 days after each quarter, through the Unified Reporting System or other electronic means, in hard copy to the MFBM, and on the ministry or office's website. A printed or electronic copy must be furnished to Parliament and to the Chairperson of the Committee on Finance, Budget and Management. The ministry must send written notice when reports have been submitted or posted, and the date of that notice counts as the date of compliance. Failure to comply results in the automatic suspension of the salaries of the responsible official or employee until they comply, pursuant to Section 57, Chapter 6, Book VI of E.O. 292. Repeated failure or refusal without justifiable cause may be a ground for administrative disciplinary action. The Minister or Head of Office is responsible for ensuring compliance with this penalty provision.
Section 4 — Takes effect immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

impact.allocated_budget: No new appropriation. It extends the FY2022 budget enacted by BAA 23 and rewrites its reporting provisions.
impact.figures_note: The act states no amount — it changes deadlines and reporting duties.

related_legislation.related_note: Amends both the cash budgeting and the quarterly reporting sections of the FY2022 General Appropriations Act. Part of the running series of validity-extension acts with BAA 14, 24, 34, 38, 51 and 52 — and the only one of them that adds a transparency mechanism.

implementation_status.irr_status: The amended Section 48 authorises the MFBM to issue implementing guidelines.
implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. The spending windows have closed; the reporting duties inserted into the FY2022 general provisions are a standing obligation on ministries.

citizen_questions.q: Where can I see what a ministry spent?
citizen_questions.a: On the ministry's own website. Section 2 requires quarterly financial and physical accomplishment reports to be posted there, as well as filed electronically and in hard copy with the finance ministry, within 30 days of each quarter's end.

citizen_questions.q: What happens if a ministry does not report?
citizen_questions.a: The salaries of the responsible official or employee are automatically suspended until they comply. Repeated failure without justifiable cause may be a ground for administrative disciplinary action.

citizen_questions.q: What happens to money that is never spent?
citizen_questions.a: Unreleased appropriations lapse, and unexpended or undisbursed funds revert to the Bangsamoro Treasury under a Special Fund for reappropriation under the Organic Law.
Most of it to 31 December 2023. Infrastructure could be completed, inspected and paid until 30 June 2024; other items until 31 March 2024. Salaries expired at the end of 2022.
Yes. A printed or electronic copy must be furnished to Parliament and to the Chairperson of the Committee on Finance, Budget and Management.
